title: Epic: SIEM-ready audit export (beta) — engineering tracker
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Goal
Ship SIEM-ready audit export (beta) for Enterprise customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Feature provides customer-configurable destinations (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, S3) with filtering, durable delivery (at-least-once), operational visibility, and replay tooling.

Scope (beta)
- New control-plane service surface for audit export: destination CRUD, credential storage, state machine (enabled/paused/degraded), and health/status.
- Delivery worker subsystem: durable buffering, checkpointing per destination, retries with exponential backoff + jitter, DLQ, and explicit failure states.
- Sink connectors: Splunk HEC (optional ACK), Datadog Logs intake (regional endpoints + throttling handling), S3 (partitioning + encryption + idempotent naming strategy).
- Filtering engine: include/exclude by event_type and selected fields (actor/resource/workspace/environment); safe defaults + validation.
- Operability: metrics, dashboards, alerts, SLOs, runbooks, and incident-bot surface area.
- Console integration is tracked separately, but this epic includes the API/health fields the Console depends on.

Non-goals (beta)
- Exactly-once delivery guarantees.
- Full historical backfill for all tenants (we will support bounded replay tooling for operators and customer-assisted backfill where needed).
- Additional SIEM vendors beyond Splunk/Datadog; customer-specific schema field mapping beyond Audit Event Schema v1.

Primary owners
- Platform control plane: Benji Okafor (implementation), Ethan Park (lead)
- Security review: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei (schema + export security)
- SRE readiness: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes
- Private packaging: Diego Santos (cross-deployment)

Key references
- PRD: confluence/product-docs/requirements/siem-ready-audit-export-beta-prd.json
- Design spec: confluence/product-docs/design-specs/audit-export-filtering-and-delivery-guarantees.json
- Schema v1: confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-event-schema-v1.json
- ADRs: adr-0217 (delivery semantics), adr-0218 (Splunk auth/ack), adr-0219 (S3 partitioning/encryption)

Milestones
1) Control plane MVP (destination model + state machine + credentials)
   - ENG-13921
   - Output: API surface usable by worker and Console; secure secret handling wired.

2) Delivery pipeline MVP (queue + worker + checkpointing + DLQ)
   - ENG-13923
   - Output: at-least-once end-to-end in staging; per-destination isolation; basic backpressure.

3) Connector MVPs (Splunk, Datadog, S3)
   - ENG-13924 / ENG-13925 / ENG-13926
   - Output: connector-specific semantics implemented and testable; error taxonomy consistent.

4) Filtering + schema v1 publication
   - ENG-13922 / ENG-13927
   - Output: stable filtering semantics and schema guidance for dedupe/correlation.

5) Operability + readiness
   - ENG-13928 / ENG-13931 / ENG-13932
   - Output: health endpoints, dashboards/alerts, defined SLOs, and load-shedding plan.

6) Security hardening + replay tooling
   - ENG-13933 / ENG-13934
   - Output: RBAC gates + audit trails + replay safeguards.

7) Private deployment packaging
   - ENG-13935
   - Output: install/upgrade notes and required egress/secrets integration validated.

Dependency graph (high level)
- ENG-13923 (queue/worker) depends on ENG-13921 (destination/credentials) and ENG-13927 (schema conventions for dedupe keys + versioning).
- Connector tasks (ENG-13924/25/26) depend on ENG-13923 (worker interface + retry/DLQ contract) and ADR decisions.
- Observability/SLO tasks (ENG-13931/32) depend on baseline metrics emitted by worker/connectors and health endpoints (ENG-13928).
- Replay tooling (ENG-13934) depends on checkpointing strategy in ENG-13923 and destination state/permissions from ENG-13921/ENG-13933.
- Private packaging (ENG-13935) depends on worker/service deployable artifacts and explicit config flags.

Engineering rollout checklist (beta)
- [ ] Feature flag plumbing per-tenant: allowlist/denylist + staged rollout plan (paired with release eng)
- [ ] Destination CRUD + credential encryption verified (KMS integration + rotation story)
- [ ] Confirm audit export config changes are themselves audited (schema event types + redaction)
- [ ] At-least-once semantics documented and reflected in connector behavior
- [ ] Dedupe guidance shipped (event_id + destination + sequence/checkpoint guidance)
- [ ] End-to-end load test at target beta QPS (including failure injection: throttling, 5xx, auth errors)
- [ ] DLQ policy: retention, operator tooling, and alert thresholds
- [ ] Backpressure/load-shedding verified: exporter cannot materially impact primary API latency
- [ ] SLOs finalized + dashboards live + paging thresholds agreed with SRE
- [ ] Runbooks complete: backlog drain, replay window, poison-pill handling, credential issues
- [ ] Private packaging validated in at least one internal sandbox cluster with restricted egress
- [ ] Security review sign-off (threat model + risk assessment mitigations implemented)
- [ ] Beta enablement plan: canary tenants + rollback conditions

Success criteria (engineering)
- 99.9% of events delivered within SLO window for healthy destinations (excluding customer endpoint outages), measured per destination.
- Clear failure modes: destination shows degraded/paused with actionable error details and correlation IDs.
- Replay tool can safely resend a bounded time window without destabilizing pipeline.
- Duplicate rate within expected bounds for at-least-once; customers can reliably dedupe with documented keys.

Open questions / watch items
- Splunk HEC ACK: default off vs on for beta? (trade-off: throughput vs stronger confirmation) — align with Kevin Osei + SRE.
- S3 idempotency strategy: object naming must avoid unbounded small objects while limiting duplicates — ensure ADR-0219 implementation matches guidance.
- Filtering DSL complexity: keep beta simple; avoid exposing raw expression language that becomes a long-term compatibility burden.

Notes
This epic is the engineering tracker and rollup. Individual implementation details should be captured in the sub-issues with PR links, test plans, and acceptance criteria.
comments: 2025-01-16 (Ethan Park): Kicked off with Security + SRE. Aligning on at-least-once messaging and explicit dedupe keys. Action: ensure schema v1 includes stable event_id and request_id semantics for SIEM correlation.

2025-01-24 (Benji Okafor): Destination model draft reviewed. Will represent per-destination state as enabled|paused|degraded and include last_success_at/last_error/backlog_estimate in read APIs for Console health.

2025-02-03 (Sean Gallagher): SRE request: exporter must have circuit breaker per destination to prevent retry storms when Splunk/Datadog returns 5xx/429. Also need DLQ alerting (rate + size) and a runbook section on poison-pill events.

2025-02-11 (Kevin Osei): Security review note: credential handling must be envelope-encrypted; no secrets in logs; audit all config changes including destination test events. Confirm RBAC permissions are enterprise-admin scoped.

2025-02-18 (Benji Okafor): Staging issue observed: connector retries saturating worker CPU under Splunk 5xx. Plan: introduce per-destination concurrency caps + jittered backoff; add metric for retry_queue_depth; update ENG-13932 scope to include destination-level circuit breaker.
